Divide a polynomial by a linear or quadratic

lines.text: The coefficients $a, b, c$ are real, so complex roots come in conjugate pairs.
$-4 + 3i$ is a root, so its conjugate is a root.
The coefficients $p, q$ are real, so complex roots come in conjugate pairs.

steps.title: Sum of the roots gives p

skill.title: Derive multiple-angle identities with De Moivre
skill.output: identity in powers of cos θ / sin θ
needs: Raise to a power with De Moivre's Theorem

steps.title: Apply de Moivre's theorem to the left side

lines.text: De Moivre's theorem: $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^n = \cos n\theta + i\sin n\theta$.
Both expressions equal $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^2$, so their real parts are equal.

skill.title: Prove De Moivre's Theorem by induction
skill.input: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ, n ∈ N
skill.example: P(k) ⇒ P(k + 1) using sin(A + B), cos(A + B)
needs: Prove a series identity by induction
Add, subtract and multiply complex numbers

lines.text: Let $P(n)$ be the statement $(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^n = \cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)$.
So $P(1)$ is true.

steps.title: Assume the result is true for n = k

lines.text: This is $P(k)$. We now test $P(k+1)$.

steps.title: Write the (k + 1) power as a product

lines.text: Replace $i^2$ with $-1$.

steps.title: Group the real and imaginary parts

lines.text: $\cos(A+B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B$ and $\sin(A+B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$, with $A = k\theta$ and $B = \theta$.
So $P(k+1)$ is true.
$P(1)$ is true. If $P(k)$ is true then $P(k+1)$ is true. Hence $P(n)$ is true for all positive integers $n$.

skill.input: f(x) and slope m (or parallel line)

steps.title: Translate the condition into a slope

lines.text: $l'(x) = \frac{1}{2}$ for every $x$, since $l$ is a straight line.
So $p'(x) = l'(x)$ means the tangent to $p$ has slope $\frac{1}{2}$, parallel to $l$.
Place a ruler along $l$ and slide it down and to the left until it just touches the curve near the lower left. Draw this tangent in blue.
Slide it up and to the right until it just touches the curve near the maximum. Draw this second tangent in blue.

steps.title: Read the x-values from the touching points

lines.text: Draw a vertical line from each touching point down to the x-axis and read off the values.
The first touches at about $x = 2.2$ and the second at about $x = 6.8$.
